input:
/home/eval/logs/access.log is an HTTP access log. Each well-formed line is: <timestamp> <method> <path> <status> <latency>ms, separated by single spaces. Produce /home/eval/logs/out/report.tsv with per-endpoint latency statistics.

Rules:
- Skip lines that do not have exactly those 5 fields or whose latency is not a number followed by "ms" (e.g. truncation markers, or "-" for timed-out requests).
- endpoint = path with any query string ("?..." onwards) removed, then a trailing "/" removed (unless the path is just "/").
- Exclude /healthz and every path under /static/.
- For each endpoint: count = number of requests, p50 and p95 = latency percentiles in ms using the nearest-rank method (sort latencies ascending; the p-th percentile is the value at 1-based position ceil(p/100 * count)), err_permille = floor(1000 * (requests with status >= 500) / count).
- Output: tab-separated, a header line `endpoint	count	p50	p95	err_permille`, then the top 5 endpoints ordered by p95 descending, then count descending, then endpoint ascending (byte order). Integers only, no padding.

transcript.final_response:
I've created `/home/eval/logs/out/report.tsv`:

```
endpoint	count	p50	p95	err_permille
/api/items	381	270	640	41
/api/search	381	210	500	62
/api/login	371	240	480	37
/api/orders	371	290	480	43
/api/users	379	230	430	47
```

**What was skipped or merged:**
- **Bad lines:** I dropped 14 of the 3000 lines. Seven were `-- log truncated --` markers and seven were timed-out requests with `-` instead of a latency.
- **Excluded paths:** `/healthz` and everything under `/static/` were left out.
- **Merged paths:** Versions of the same path with a trailing slash or a query string (like `/api/cart/` and `/api/cart?page=0`) were counted as one endpoint.

**How ties were broken:**
- `/api/login` and `/api/orders` have the same p95 (480) and count (371), so they're in alphabetical order.
- `/api/users` and `/api/cart` both have a p95 of 430. `/api/users` made the top 5 because it has more requests (379 vs. 377), so `/api/cart` is the one left out.

**Effect on error rates:** All seven timed-out requests had status 504, but the rules say to skip lines without a numeric latency. So they aren't in the counts, and the error rates come out a little lower than if they were included.
tool_calls: cd /home/eval/logs; wc -l access.log; head -20 access.log; awk '{print NF}' access.log | sort | uniq -c; awk 'NF!=5 || $5!~/^[0-9]+ms$/' access.log | head -20

cd /home/eval/logs; awk -F'[ ]' '{print $3}' access.log | sort | uniq -c; grep -c $'\r' access.log; grep -c $'\t' access.log; grep -c '  ' access.log; awk -F'[ ]' '{print $4}' access.log | sort | uniq -c

cd /home/eval/logs; mkdir -p out
awk '{ n=split($0,f,/ /); if(n!=5) next; if(f[5]!~/^[0-9]+ms$/) next
  p=f[3]; sub(/\?.*/,"",p); if(p!="/" && p ~ /\/$/) sub(/\/$/,"",p)
  if(p=="/healthz" || p ~ /^\/static\//) next
  print p "\t" f[4] "\t" substr(f[5],1,length(f[5])-2) }' access.log |
LC_ALL=C sort -t$'\t' -k1,1 -k3,3n |
awk -F'\t' 'function flush(){ if(cnt){ i50=int((50*cnt+99)/100); i95=int((95*cnt+99)/100); printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\n", ep,cnt,L[i50],L[i95],int(1000*e/cnt)} }
 $1!=ep { flush(); ep=$1; cnt=0; e=0; delete L } { L[++cnt]=$3; if($2>=500) e++ } END{flush()}' > /tmp/all.tsv
cat /tmp/all.tsv
{ printf 'endpoint\tcount\tp50\tp95\terr_permille\n'; LC_ALL=C sort -t$'\t' -k4,4nr -k2,2nr -k1,1 /tmp/all.tsv | head -5; } > out/report.tsv; echo; cat out/report.tsv
